title: What If Russia Nuked Lithuania? The First 61 Hours
description:
What would a Russian nuclear strike on Lithuania look like if a war with NATO went nuclear? This simulation follows the first 61 hours of a Russian attack on the Baltic states, built from published wargames and force data, to one 10-kiloton warhead over one air base, ring by ring.

Three forty-three in the morning, Lithuania: a radar picks up one ballistic missile climbing out of Kaliningrad, aimed at Siauliai Air Base. Nobody on the ground can tell whether the warhead is conventional or nuclear, and the flight is about three minutes. Why would Moscow fire it, and what does the world do in the hour after?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. It is not a forecast and uses no real date. The drone alerts of 11 November 2026, the 2025 airspace incidents, the 1995 Norwegian rocket false alarm and the arsenal figures are real; scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen, facts REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY. Our choices: the strike list, the launch sites, the timeline and the 10-kiloton yield (we found no published Iskander yield).

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:38 A night of sirens
2:15 How close it has come
3:32 The trigger
4:48 Hour by hour
6:57 One warhead, ring by ring
8:17 The day after

Key sources
- Al Jazeera, Russia warns NATO of a nuclear response if Kaliningrad is cut off (2026): https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/30/russia-warns-nato-of-possible-nuclear-response-if-kaliningrad-is-cut-off
- Al-Monitor, Baltic nations issue drone warnings (2026-11-11): https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/baltic-nations-finland-issue-overnight-drone-warnings-russia-ukraine-exchange
- RAND, Reinforcing Deterrence on NATO's Eastern Flank (2016): https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RR1253.html
- Arms Control Association, Plan A: how nuclear war could progress (Princeton): https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2020-07/features/plan-how-nuclear-war-could-progress
- Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Russian nuclear weapons 2026: https://thebulletin.org/premium/2026-05/russian-nuclear-weapons-2026/
- CRS, Russian nuclear weapons (2026): https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-05-27_IF12672_25c6e3a8d3ac199781b27c13fe5da5547ce070b7.html
- NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty: https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/official_texts_17120.htm
- Norwegian rocket incident (1995): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_rocket_incident
Blast and burn figures: the channel's scenario engine, from Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the attack timeline, the targets, the launch sites and the yield are ours, a scenario, not a forecast.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble; thumbnail backgrounds generated with Google Gemini. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
